ra: Dabog is a South-Slavic high deity belonging to the broader Slavic pantheon hub.
Dabog is the South-Slavic (Serbian) cognate/reflex of the East-Slavic sun-god Dažbog; same theonym (modern cognate => aligned_with since cognate_of is unavailable).
In Serbian folk tradition Dabog is a chthonic lord of underground wealth, a role overlapping the chthonic Veles.
The vile are a South-Slavic class of nature-spirits within the Slavic domestic-and-nature-spirit grouping.
Vile are the South-Slavic functional counterpart of the East-Slavic Rusalka water/nature nymphs, but a distinct class (homonym caution noted).
German is a folk ritual fertility/rain figure within the Slavic folk-spirit complex.
The German rain-effigy rite parallels other Slavic seasonal effigy/agrarian rites such as the Kupala observances.
Vid is a reconstructed South-Slavic theonym placed within the Slavic pantheon.
Vid shares the -vit theophoric element and light/sky associations with the West-Slavic Svetovit (Sventovit).
Prove is a Polabian Slavic god belonging to the Slavic pantheon hub.
Pripegala is a Polabian Slavic deity assigned to the Slavic pantheon hub.
Tjarnaglofi is a Pomeranian Slavic war-god belonging to the Slavic pantheon hub.
Tjarnaglofi was a Rani (Rügen-area) war-idol alongside the other West-Slavic war-gods such as Rugievit.
